q: A Stores Tender Committee is considering a high-value purchase case. To ensure financial scrutiny of the proposal within the committee itself, the committee includes a member from the:
e: A Stores Tender Committee includes a member from the Finance and Accounts Department to ensure financial scrutiny of high-value purchase proposals within the committee itself.

q: An indent for procurement of a non-stock item is sent for Finance vetting before purchase action is taken. The vetting is directed principally to ensuring:

options.A: That the material will be inspected by RDSO
options.B: Availability of funds and the propriety of the demand
options.C: That the supplier is registered with NSIC
options.D: That the lowest tenderer is selected by the committee

e: Finance vetting of an indent for a non-stock item is directed principally to availability of funds and propriety of the demand before purchase action is taken.

q: A firm holds a rate (running) contract for an item of stores. During the currency of the contract, the depots obtain their supplies from the firm by:

options.A: Inviting fresh tenders for every requirement
options.B: Taking the entire estimated quantity in one lot at the start
options.C: Placing supply orders on the firm from time to time, as and when required, at the contract rate
options.D: Purchasing from the open market and debiting the firm

e: Under a rate or running contract, depots place supply orders on the firm from time to time as required, at the contract rate, without inviting fresh tenders for each requirement.

q: An item is a proprietary article and is covered by a Proprietary Article Certificate (PAC). Procurement of such an article is made through:
e: An article covered by a Proprietary Article Certificate is procured through single tender, since it is a proprietary article available from a specific source.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Reverse auction on IREPS is used by the Railways for purchase of stores.
2. E-auction on IREPS is used by the Railways for disposal of scrap.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: reverse auction on IREPS is used for purchase of stores, and e-auction on IREPS is used for disposal of scrap.

q: The closing balance of stores of a railway at the end of a year is Rs 96 lakh and the total issues of stores during the year are Rs 480 lakh. The Turnover Ratio of stores of the railway is:
e: Turnover Ratio = closing balance divided by total issues = Rs 96 lakh / Rs 480 lakh = 0.20.

q: The annual requirement of an item is 7,200 units and it is ordered in Economic Order Quantities of 600 units. If the cost of placing one order is Rs 250, the total ordering cost per year is:
e: Number of orders per year = 7,200 / 600 = 12. Total ordering cost = 12 x Rs 250 = Rs 3,000.

q: The average consumption of an item is 90 units per week and the lead time for its procurement is 8 weeks. The consumption of the item during the lead time is:
e: Consumption during lead time = average consumption x lead time = 90 units per week x 8 weeks = 720 units.

q: The Average Annual Consumption (AAC) of an item is 7,200 units. Coverage for five months is required to be provided. The stock in hand is 1,100 units and the dues (quantity already on order) are 700 units. The quantity to be ordered is:
e: Five months requirement is 7,200 / 12 x 5 = 3,000 units. Less stock in hand and dues of 1,100 + 700 = 1,800 units, the quantity to order is 1,200 units.

q: An imported stores item is invoiced at Rs 3,50,000. The freight paid on it is Rs 28,000, the insurance premium Rs 7,000 and the customs duty Rs 42,000. The value at which the item is taken into stock, on landed cost basis, is:
e: Landed cost = invoice price + freight + insurance + customs duty = Rs 3,50,000 + Rs 28,000 + Rs 7,000 + Rs 42,000 = Rs 4,27,000.

q: A supplier fails to supply 500 units of stores contracted at Rs 120 per unit. A risk purchase of the same quantity is made at Rs 155 per unit. The extra cost recoverable from the defaulting supplier is:
e: Extra cost of risk purchase = (Rs 155 - Rs 120) x 500 units = Rs 35 x 500 = Rs 17,500, recoverable from the defaulting supplier.

q: A depot issues 600 units of an item, whose book rate is Rs 75 per unit, to an outside party. Departmental charges are leviable at 10 per cent of the book value. The total amount recoverable from the party is:
e: Book value is 600 x Rs 75 = Rs 45,000. Adding departmental charges at 10 per cent, Rs 4,500, the total recoverable is Rs 49,500.

q: During stock verification, 25 units of an item are found in excess of the book balance. The book rate of the item is Rs 180 per unit. The value of the excess taken into stock through the Stock Adjustment Account is:
e: Excess found on stock verification is taken into stock at book rate through the Stock Adjustment Account: 25 units x Rs 180 = Rs 4,500.

q: A depot holds 950 units of an item whose book rate is revised from Rs 52 to Rs 58 per unit. The increase in the value of the stock in hand, which is adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account, is:
e: The rise in book rate is Rs 58 - Rs 52 = Rs 6 per unit. On 950 units the stock value rises by 950 x Rs 6 = Rs 5,700, adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account.

q: Stores of the value of Rs 2,00,000 are supplied three weeks late by a supplier. Liquidated damages are leviable at 0.5 per cent of the value of the stores in arrear for each week of delay. The liquidated damages recoverable are:
e: LD at 0.5 per cent per week for 3 weeks = 1.5 per cent of the value in arrear of Rs 2,00,000 = Rs 3,000.

q: A supplier's stores bill amounts to Rs 4,50,000. Advance payment is made at 98 per cent of the bill amount against the inspection certificate and despatch documents. The amount of advance payment is:
e: Advance payment at 98 per cent of Rs 4,50,000 = Rs 4,41,000, made against the inspection certificate and despatch documents.

q: A purchaser of a scrap lot delays lifting the material for 9 days beyond the delivery period allowed to him. Ground rent is leviable at Rs 550 per day for the period of delay. The total ground rent payable by him is:
e: Ground rent for delayed lifting = 9 days x Rs 550 per day = Rs 4,950, as per the conditions of sale.

q: A purchase order is placed for stores valued at Rs 8,40,000. The security deposit prescribed in the contract, at 10 per cent of the order value, works out to:
e: Security deposit at 10 per cent of the order value of Rs 8,40,000 = Rs 84,000.

q: The average value of the inventory held by a railway is Rs 60 lakh and the inventory carrying cost is estimated at 18 per cent per annum of the stock value. The inventory carrying cost per year is:
e: Annual inventory carrying cost = 18 per cent of the average stock value of Rs 60 lakh = Rs 10,80,000.

q: An item has a safety stock of 200 units and its Economic Order Quantity is 800 units. Under the EOQ system, the maximum inventory of the item will be:
e: Under the EOQ system, maximum inventory = safety stock + Economic Order Quantity = 200 + 800 = 1,000 units.

q:
Consider the following statements about the stock levels of an item:
1. The safety (buffer) stock of an item is ordinarily consumed and exhausted before every fresh receipt of the item arrives.
2. The re-order level of an item is fixed at the consumption during the lead time plus the safety (buffer) stock, the buffer being held to absorb variations in consumption and in lead time.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 2 alone is correct: re-order level is lead-time consumption plus safety stock, the buffer being held against variations; the buffer is not ordinarily consumed and exhausted before every receipt.

q: A purchaser deposits the full sale value of a scrap lot with the Railways, but the scrap has not yet been delivered to him. Until delivery is effected, this position is reflected in the stores accounts by a balance under Sales Suspense which is a:

options.A: Debit balance, indicating sale value deposited but material not yet delivered
options.B: Credit balance, indicating material received but bills not paid
options.D: Credit balance under Stock Adjustment Account

e: Sale value deposited by the purchaser but material not yet delivered leaves a debit balance under Sales Suspense, indicating the position until delivery is effected.

q: Material has been received at a depot and taken into stock, but the supplier's bill for the material has not yet been paid. In the stores accounts, this position gives rise to a balance under Purchase Suspense which is a:
e: Material received and taken into stock but the supplier's bill not yet paid gives a credit balance under Purchase Suspense, which is cleared on payment of the bill.

q: An item held in a depot has not been issued at all during the last 26 months, and on review it is not expected to be used during the next 24 months. The item is correctly classified as:
e: Stores not issued at all during the last 24 months, here 26 months, and not expected to be used during the next 24 months are classified as dead surplus stores.

q: In a stores tender governed by the Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order, a supplier offers an item with a local content of 35 per cent. The supplier is classified as a:
e: Under the Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order, local content of 20 per cent or more but less than 50 per cent, here 35 per cent, makes a Class-II local supplier.

q: A railway plans annual procurement of goods and services of Rs 12 crore. Applying the prescribed minimum percentage of procurement to be made from Micro and Small Enterprises, the minimum value to be procured from such enterprises is:
e: Minimum procurement from Micro and Small Enterprises is 25 per cent of Rs 12 crore = Rs 3.00 crore.

q: In the two-bid system of stores tendering, the techno-commercial bid of a firm is opened and the firm is found not to qualify technically. The correct course in respect of that firm's price bid is that it:

options.A: Is opened along with the price bids of qualified bidders
options.B: Is opened first, before the technical evaluation is completed
options.C: Is not opened, price bids of only technically qualified bidders being opened
options.D: Is opened after negotiation with the firm

e: In the two-bid system the price bid of a firm that does not qualify technically is not opened; price bids of only technically qualified bidders are opened.

q: In a stores tender, negotiations, where they become unavoidable in exceptional circumstances, are held:

options.D: With the tenderer who quoted the estimated rate

e: Negotiations in stores tenders, where unavoidable in exceptional circumstances, are held only with the lowest tenderer, L1.

q: A stores tenderer submitted an offer with a validity period which has since expired, and the Railway now wishes to accept the offer. The acceptance can be communicated to the tenderer:

options.A: At any time, as validity is of no consequence after opening
options.C: Only after approval of the Railway Board in every such case
options.D: Only with the consent of the tenderer, the validity period having expired

e: Once the validity period of an offer has expired, the offer can be accepted only with the consent of the tenderer.

q: During the currency of a stores contract, the contractor sells the same item to another buyer at a rate lower than the rate in the railway contract. Under the fall clause of the contract:

options.A: The railway contract is automatically terminated
options.B: The lower rate shall apply to the railway contract also
options.C: The Railway must pay the higher contract rate in all cases
options.D: The contractor is banned from all future railway business

e: Under the fall clause, a lower rate at which the contractor sells the same item to another buyer during the contract applies to the railway contract also.

q: A clause in a stores contract is invoked to verify the costs and prices claimed by the contractor by looking into his books of account. The clause so invoked is the:
e: The book examination clause is invoked to verify the costs and prices claimed by the contractor by examining his books of account relating to the contract.

q: The same stores item is held in two different depots of a railway, and a consuming department asks why the item is issued to it at the same rate from both depots. The correct explanation is that, under uniform pricing on the railway:

options.A: All items in stock carry the same price
options.B: All suppliers quote identical rates to the railway
options.C: The issue (book) rate of an item is the same in all depots of the railway
options.D: Issue prices are revised in every depot every day

e: Under uniform pricing, the issue or book rate of an item is the same in all depots of the railway, so a consuming department is charged at the same rate from either depot.

q: Book balances of every stores item in a depot are maintained continuously and the balances are physically verified in rotation. The system of stores accounting so described is the:
e: The perpetual inventory system maintains book balances of every item continuously and verifies them physically in rotation, unlike periodic annual stock-taking.

q: The stock of an item in a depot has fallen below the minimum level fixed for it, to a level at which emergency action to replenish the stock must be taken. The level so reached is the:
e: The danger level is the level below the minimum at which stock has fallen so low that emergency action to replenish it must be taken.

q: The re-order level of an item is 1,000 units and its re-order quantity is 600 units. The minimum consumption of the item is 40 units per week and the minimum lead time is 5 weeks. The maximum stock level of the item is:
e: Maximum stock level = re-order level + re-order quantity - (minimum consumption x minimum lead time) = 1,000 + 600 - (40 x 5) = 1,600 - 200 = 1,400 units.

q: A costly, slow-moving spare is stocked in a depot solely to guard against a prolonged breakdown of an important item of equipment, although it may not be drawn for a long time. Such a spare is correctly described as an:
e: A costly slow-moving spare stocked solely to guard against prolonged breakdown of important equipment, though it may not be drawn for long, is an insurance spare.

q: A stores item is classified in a depot as a vital item. The distinguishing feature of such an item is that:

options.A: Its non-availability can affect the safe running of trains
options.B: It is the costliest item held in the depot
options.C: It is consumed in the largest quantity every day
options.D: It is procured only from a foreign supplier

e: A vital item is distinguished by the fact that its non-availability can affect the safe running of trains, not by its price or quantity consumed.

q: Tools and plant are issued from a depot to a department for use on a work, against acknowledgement, and are required to be returned to stores after use. Such stores are known as:
e: Tools and plant issued to a department against acknowledgement and required to be returned to stores after use are known as returnable stores.

q: The charge of a stores depot is transferred from one custodian to another. The correct procedure for the incoming custodian is to:

options.A: Take over on book balances alone, without any check of the stores
options.B: Take over only the A-category items and leave the rest unchecked
options.C: Refuse charge until the next annual stock verification falls due
options.D: Take over the stores after verification of balances, with discrepancies, if any, brought on record

e: On transfer of charge of a stores depot, the incoming custodian takes over the stores after verification of balances, with any discrepancies brought on record.

q: Stores are held in the custody of a user department at an outstation, outside the stores depots. The physical verification of such departmentally held stores is carried out by:

options.A: The depot storekeeper of the nearest stores depot
options.B: The Accounts Stock Verifiers in every case
options.C: Officers of the department holding the stores
options.D: The Travelling Inspector of Stores Accounts

e: Stores held in the custody of a user department outside the stores depots are physically verified by officers of the department holding the stores.

q: A half-yearly statement of stores accounts is under preparation in the Accounts office. The essential purpose of the Balance Sheet of Stores Accounts so prepared is to show:

options.A: Only the attendance position of stores staff for the half year
options.B: Only the list of tenders opened during the half year
options.C: Only the dues recoverable from suppliers of stores
options.D: The balances under stock and suspense heads, proving the agreement of the priced ledger with the general books

e: The Balance Sheet of Stores Accounts shows the balances under stock and suspense heads, proving agreement of the priced stores ledger with the general books of the railway.

q: Stores have been issued from a depot to another railway and the value of the issue is awaiting final adjustment and recovery from that railway. Pending such adjustment, the value is accommodated in the stores accounts under the:
e: Value of stores issued to another railway, pending final adjustment and recovery from that railway, is accommodated under the Stores Miscellaneous Suspense head.

q: A Government buyer requires a common-use office item which is available from sellers listed on an online marketplace, while a railway-specific stores item is to be procured by tendering. The correct pairing of the requirement with the portal is:

options.A: Both items are procured only through IREPS
options.B: The common-use item is procured through GeM and the railway-specific item through tendering on IREPS
options.C: Both items are procured only through GeM
options.D: The common-use item is procured through IREPS and the railway-specific item through GeM

e: Common-use items available on an online marketplace are procured through GeM, while railway-specific stores items are procured by tendering on IREPS.

q: A registered vendor's supplies are repeatedly found defective and its deliveries are persistently delayed, and its performance rating is consequently poor. The action that may be taken against the firm in respect of its registration is:

options.A: Allotment of larger orders to the firm as compensation
options.B: Imposition of a fine personally by the depot storekeeper
options.C: No consequence, as registration once granted cannot be disturbed
options.D: Down-gradation, suspension or cancellation of its registration

e: For repeated defective supplies and persistent delays reflected in a poor performance rating, a registered vendor's registration may be down-graded, suspended or cancelled.

q: Stores supplied under a contract are found defective within the warranty period and the supplier, though called upon, fails to replace or repair them. The course open to the Railway is to:

options.A: Bear the cost of repair itself and drop the claim against the supplier
options.B: Throw away the defective stores without any recovery
options.C: Arrange the repair or replacement at the supplier's risk and cost and recover the amount from his dues or security deposit
options.D: Wait indefinitely until the supplier chooses to act

e: If a supplier fails to replace or repair defective stores within the warranty period, the Railway may arrange repair or replacement at the supplier's risk and cost and recover it from his dues or security deposit.

q: Stores are imported under a Letter of Credit opened in favour of the foreign supplier. Payment to the supplier under the Letter of Credit is made:

options.A: Only after the material is received and verified in the Indian depot
options.B: In cash to the supplier's agent at the Indian port of entry
options.C: Only after the close of the financial year of the order
options.D: Against presentation of the stipulated shipping documents through the bank, and not on physical receipt of the material in India

e: Under a Letter of Credit, payment to the foreign supplier is made against presentation of the stipulated shipping documents through the bank, not on physical receipt of the material in India.

q: Stores returned to a depot by a work are examined and found unfit for immediate issue, but capable of being made serviceable again after repair in a workshop. The returned stores are correctly classified as:

options.B: Serviceable stores fit for immediate issue

e: Returned stores unfit for immediate issue but capable of being made serviceable after workshop repair are classified as repairable stores.

q: A consuming department wishes to plan its demand for a stores item. Through the user depot module of iMMS, the department can:

options.A: Pass suppliers' bills for payment on behalf of Accounts
options.B: Conduct the e-auction of scrap lots of the depot
options.C: View the stock position of the item in depots and raise its demand online
options.D: Fix the Average Annual Consumption of A-category items

e: Through the user depot module of iMMS, a consuming department can view the stock position of an item in depots and raise its demand online.

q: For a stock item, the stock in hand together with the dues (quantity already on order) is assessed against the expected consumption of the item. The period for which the stock in hand and on order will meet the consumption requirements of the item is known as its:
e: Coverage is the period for which the stock in hand together with dues on order will meet the expected consumption requirements of an item.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Dead and surplus stock contributes fully to issues and therefore does not add to the inventory carrying cost of a railway.
2. Reducing obsolete and surplus stock is an objective of inventory control, partly because it cuts the inventory carrying cost.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 2 alone is correct: reducing obsolete and surplus stock is an objective of inventory control and cuts carrying cost, while dead and surplus stock does not contribute fully to issues and does add to carrying cost.

q: The closing balance of stores of a railway is Rs 88 lakh and the total issues of stores during the year are Rs 4 crore. The Turnover Ratio of the stores is:
e: Turnover Ratio is closing balance divided by total issues. Rs 88 lakh divided by Rs 4 crore (Rs 400 lakh) gives 0.22, showing stock equal to about 22 per cent of a year's issues.

q: The opening balance of stores of a railway is Rs 55 lakh, receipts of stores during the year are Rs 1.85 crore and issues during the year are Rs 1.72 crore. The closing balance of stores is:
e: Closing balance equals opening balance plus receipts minus issues: 55 + 185 - 172 = Rs 68 lakh. This is the basic stores account equation under the Stores Code.

q: The annual consumption of an item is 4,050 units. The cost of placing one order is Rs 100 and the inventory carrying cost is Rs 4 per unit per year. The Economic Order Quantity is:
e: EOQ equals square root of (2 x annual consumption x ordering cost / carrying cost) = square root of (2 x 4050 x 100 / 4) = square root of 2,02,500 = 450 units.

q: A depot holds 250 units of an item at a book rate of Rs 36 per unit. A fresh receipt of 150 units is taken into stock at Rs 52 per unit. The revised book (average) rate of the item will be:
e: Revised average rate equals total value divided by total quantity: (250 x 36 + 150 x 52) / 400 = 16,800 / 400 = Rs 42 per unit. Issues are priced at this average book rate.

q: The AAC of an item is 8,400 units. The stock in hand is 1,050 units and the dues (quantity already on order) are 350 units. The coverage available for the item is:
e: Coverage equals (stock in hand plus dues) divided by monthly consumption. Monthly AAC is 8400 / 12 = 700; (1050 + 350) / 700 = 2 months.

q: The AAC of a stock item is 6,600 units and coverage for five months is to be provided. The stock in hand is 800 units and the dues are 200 units. The quantity to be ordered is:
e: Quantity for 5 months is 6600 / 12 x 5 = 2750 units. Less stock 800 and dues 200 already available, the quantity to be ordered is 2750 - 1000 = 1750 units.

q: The average consumption of an item is 140 units per week, the lead time is 5 weeks and the safety (buffer) stock is 420 units. The re-order level of the item is:
e: Re-order level equals average consumption during lead time plus safety stock: 140 x 5 + 420 = 700 + 420 = 1120 units.

q: The re-order level of a stock item is 1,240 units. Its average consumption is 110 units per week and the average lead time is 8 weeks. The minimum stock level of the item is:
e: Minimum level equals re-order level minus average consumption during average lead time: 1240 - (110 x 8) = 1240 - 880 = 360 units.

q: The re-order level of an item is 1,450 units and the re-order quantity is 1,050 units. The minimum consumption is 65 units per week and the minimum lead time is 5 weeks. The maximum stock level of the item is:
e: Maximum level equals re-order level plus re-order quantity minus minimum consumption during minimum lead time: 1450 + 1050 - (65 x 5) = 2500 - 325 = 2175 units.

q: The average consumption of an item is 72 units per day and the lead time for its emergency procurement, as given, is 6 days. The danger level of the item is:
e: Danger level equals average consumption multiplied by the emergency procurement lead time: 72 x 6 = 432 units, the level at which urgent action is needed.

q: The minimum level of an item is 640 units and the maximum level is 2,360 units. The average stock level of the item is:
e: Average stock level equals (minimum level plus maximum level) / 2 = (640 + 2360) / 2 = 1500 units.

q: The average value of stock held by a railway is Rs 95 lakh. If the inventory carrying cost is estimated at 12 per cent per annum of the average stock value, the annual inventory carrying cost is:
e: Inventory carrying cost is a percentage of average stock value: 12 per cent of Rs 95 lakh = Rs 11.4 lakh per annum.

q: During stock verification, a shortage of 42 units of an item is found. The book rate of the item is Rs 260 per unit. The value of the shortage to be accounted for is:
e: Shortage value is quantity short multiplied by book rate: 42 x Rs 260 = Rs 10,920, accounted for through a stock sheet and the Stock Adjustment Account.

q: During stock verification, 18 units of an item are found physically in excess of the book balance. The book rate of the item is Rs 725 per unit. The value of the excess to be accounted for is:
e: Excess value is quantity in excess multiplied by book rate: 18 x Rs 725 = Rs 13,050, taken on stock through a stock sheet and the Stock Adjustment Account.

q: Under a stores contract, stores of the value of Rs 3,60,000 remain in arrear of supply and are supplied 5 weeks late. Liquidated damages at 0.5 per cent of the value of the stores in arrear for each week of delay amount to:
e: LD is 0.5 per cent of Rs 3,60,000 = Rs 1,800 per week. For 5 weeks of delay, LD = 1800 x 5 = Rs 9,000, as per the liquidated damages clause of the contract.

q: The value of a stores contract is Rs 72 lakh. The maximum liquidated damages recoverable under the contract, at the ceiling of 10 per cent of the contract value, is:
e: LD is capped at 10 per cent of contract value under the standard conditions of contract: 10 per cent of Rs 72 lakh = Rs 7.2 lakh maximum.

q: Advance payment at 98 per cent of the value of stores has been made on a supplier's bill of Rs 7,50,000 against the inspection certificate and despatch documents. The balance payable after the material is received, inspected and accepted at destination is:
e: Balance payable is 100 - 98 = 2 per cent of Rs 7,50,000 = Rs 15,000, paid only after receipt, inspection and acceptance of material at destination.

q: A supplier defaults on a purchase order for 1,250 units at Rs 88 per unit, and the Railway makes a risk purchase of the same quantity at Rs 103 per unit. The excess cost recoverable from the defaulting supplier is:
e: Risk purchase excess is (risk rate minus contract rate) x quantity: (103 - 88) x 1250 = 15 x 1250 = Rs 18,750, recoverable from the defaulting supplier under the risk purchase clause.

q: A depot issues 425 units of an item, whose book rate is Rs 96 per unit, to an outside party. Departmental charges are leviable at 11 per cent of the book value. The total amount recoverable from the party is:
e: Book value is 425 x 96 = Rs 40,800. Adding departmental charges at 11 per cent (Rs 4,488) gives total recoverable Rs 45,288 for issues to outside parties.

q: An imported stores item is invoiced at Rs 6,20,000. The freight paid on it is Rs 52,000, the insurance premium Rs 13,000 and the customs duty Rs 85,000. The landed cost at which the item is taken into stock is:
e: Landed cost includes invoice price plus freight, insurance and customs duty: 6,20,000 + 52,000 + 13,000 + 85,000 = Rs 7,70,000, at which imported stores are taken into stock.

q: Nine wagons loaded with stores are detained at a depot for 4 days beyond the free time allowed for unloading. Demurrage is payable at Rs 750 per wagon per day. The total demurrage payable is:
e: Demurrage equals wagons x days x rate: 9 x 4 x Rs 750 = Rs 27,000 for detention beyond the free time allowed for unloading.

q: A purchaser of a scrap lot delays lifting the material for 14 days beyond the delivery period allowed to him. Ground rent is leviable at Rs 475 per day. The total ground rent leviable is:
e: Ground rent equals days of delayed lifting x daily rate: 14 x Rs 475 = Rs 6,650, leviable under the conditions of sale of scrap.

q: A field official holds a stores imprest of a fixed quantity of 1,100 units of an item. At the time of replenishment he holds 420 units on hand and renders an account of the consumption. The quantity to be replenished is:
e: Imprest is restored to its fixed quantity, so replenishment equals fixed quantity minus stock on hand: 1100 - 420 = 680 units, against the account of consumption rendered.

q: The annual requirement of an item is 11,400 units and the quantity ordered each time, as given, is 950 units. The number of orders placed for the item during the year is:
e: Number of orders equals annual requirement divided by quantity per order: 11,400 / 950 = 12 orders in the year.

q: Orders for an item are placed in Economic Order Quantities, and the annual ordering cost of the item works out to Rs 3,600. On the principle on which the Economic Order Quantity is based, the annual inventory carrying cost of the item at that quantity is:
e: EOQ is fixed where annual ordering cost equals annual carrying cost, so if ordering cost is Rs 3,600, the carrying cost at EOQ is also Rs 3,600.

q: The safety (buffer) stock of an item is 275 units and the inventory carrying cost is Rs 18 per unit per year. The annual cost of carrying the safety stock is:
e: Annual cost of carrying safety stock equals safety stock x carrying cost per unit: 275 x Rs 18 = Rs 4,950.

q: The Purchase Suspense account of a railway opens with a debit balance of Rs 7 lakh. During the month, bills amounting to Rs 52 lakh are paid and material received against bills paid amounts to Rs 47 lakh. The closing balance of the account is:

options.A: A credit balance of Rs 12 lakh
options.B: A debit balance of Rs 5 lakh
options.C: A debit balance of Rs 12 lakh

e: Purchase Suspense closing debit equals opening debit plus bills paid minus material received and linked: 7 + 52 - 47 = Rs 12 lakh debit, representing payments awaiting linked receipts.

q: During a year, the Stock Adjustment Account of a railway is debited with Rs 2,75,000 on account of shortages and Rs 45,000 on account of downward revisions of book rates, and credited with Rs 60,000 on account of excesses found and Rs 30,000 on account of upward revisions of book rates. The net balance of the account for the year is:
e: Debits are 2,75,000 + 45,000 = Rs 3,20,000; credits are 60,000 + 30,000 = Rs 90,000. Net balance is a debit of 3,20,000 - 90,000 = Rs 2,30,000 in the Stock Adjustment Account.

q: A lot of scrap having a book value of Rs 1,35,000 is sold by e-auction for Rs 1,62,000. The difference between the sale value and the book value is dealt with in the stores accounts by:

options.A: Crediting Rs 27,000 to the Stock Adjustment Account
options.B: Debiting Rs 27,000 to the Purchase Suspense Account
options.C: Crediting Rs 1,62,000 to the Sales Suspense Account
options.D: Debiting Rs 1,35,000 to the Stock Adjustment Account

e: Sale value Rs 1,62,000 exceeds book value Rs 1,35,000 by Rs 27,000. This profit on sale of scrap is credited to the Stock Adjustment Account; the sale value itself passes through Sales Suspense.

q: A depot holds 2,750 units of an item whose book rate is revised from Rs 38 to Rs 46 per unit. The increase in the value of the stock in hand, adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account, is:
e: Increase in stock value equals quantity x rise in rate: 2750 x (46 - 38) = 2750 x 8 = Rs 22,000, adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account.

q: A newly posted stores official asks what field of work the Indian Railway Stores Code, as a whole, covers. The correct answer is that the Code deals with:

options.A: Only the compilation of the stores accounts of a railway
options.B: Only the purchase of stores through tenders and contracts
options.C: The purchase, receipt, custody, issue, accounting and disposal of stores
options.D: Only the disposal of scrap and surplus stores by auction

e: The Indian Railway Stores Code covers the full cycle of stores work: purchase, receipt, custody, issue, accounting and disposal of stores, not any one stage alone.

q: An objection is raised that the stores accounts of a railway have been audited by an authority having no locus in the matter. The audit of railway stores accounts is in fact carried out by:

options.A: The Stores Tender Committee of the railway
options.B: A chartered accountant engaged by the suppliers of stores
options.C: The depot storekeeper holding the stores
options.D: The Railway Audit organisation working under the Comptroller and Auditor General of India

e: Railway stores accounts are audited by the Railway Audit organisation under the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, which audits all Government accounts.

q: A depot officer proposes to insure the stores held in his depot commercially against fire and theft. The correct position under the rules of financial propriety is that:

options.A: Government property, including railway stores, is not insured commercially, Government bearing its own risk of loss
options.B: Commercial insurance of all depot stock is compulsory
options.C: Only stores costing above Rs 1 lakh are required to be insured commercially
options.D: The depot officer must insure the stock at his personal cost

e: Under the rules of financial propriety, Government bears its own risk and Government property, including railway stores, is not insured commercially against fire or theft.

q: A depot holds the same class of fitting in a large number of slightly differing sizes and patterns, and a programme of standardisation and variety reduction is taken up for such items. The programme is aimed principally at:

options.A: Increase the number of varieties of items held in stock
options.B: Reduce the number of items and varieties held in stock, thereby reducing inventory and simplifying procurement
options.C: Dispense with the inspection of purchased stores
options.D: Ensure that every item is purchased from a single firm only

e: Standardisation and variety reduction cut the number of items and varieties stocked, which reduces inventory holding and simplifies procurement and maintenance.

q: Copper and brass fittings held in a depot are valuable items which are prone to pilferage. Such 'attractive' stores are required to be kept:

options.A: On open racks accessible to all depot staff
options.B: In the scrap yard along with condemned stores
options.C: Under special lock and key, with restricted access
options.D: Permanently in the custody of the consuming departments

e: Attractive stores like copper and brass fittings are prone to pilferage, so the Stores Code requires them to be kept under special lock and key with restricted access.

q: Petrol, oils and paints held in a stores depot are inflammable in nature. Such stores are required to be stored:

options.A: Along with the general stores in any ward of the depot
options.B: In the open yard without any protection
options.C: In the office room of the depot officer
options.D: Separately, in specially protected accommodation, away from other stores

e: Inflammable stores such as petrol, oils and paints must be stored separately in specially protected accommodation away from other stores, as a fire safety rule.

q:
Consider the following statements about stores having a limited shelf life, such as rubber goods and paints:
1. Such stores deteriorate or expire with the passage of time.
2. Special watch is required over such stores so that they are consumed before their shelf life expires.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: shelf-life stores deteriorate or expire with time, so special watch is kept to ensure they are consumed before their shelf life expires.

q: The full sale value of an e-auction lot stands deposited by the purchaser and he now presents himself at the depot to take the material away. The depot authorises the handing over of the material to him through:

options.A: A fresh purchase order placed on the purchaser
options.C: A stock sheet prepared by the stock verifier
options.D: A tender notice issued by the depot

e: Material sold in e-auction is handed over to the purchaser, after full payment, under a delivery order issued by the depot; no fresh purchase order or tender is involved.

q: Stores are stolen from a depot godown during the night. In addition to reporting the matter to the departmental authorities, the theft is required to be reported to:

options.A: The firm which supplied the stores

e: Theft of stores must be reported to the RPF/Police for investigation, in addition to departmental authorities, so the loss can be enquired into and responsibility fixed.

q: A custodian of stores detects a shortage of stores in his charge. The correct action for him is to:

options.A: Wait until the next annual stock verification before reporting the shortage
options.B: Make good the shortage quietly, without reporting it to anyone
options.C: Sell other surplus stores in the depot to cover up the shortage
options.D: Report the loss promptly to the controlling officer/Accounts, so that an enquiry into it can be ordered

e: A custodian detecting a shortage must report the loss promptly to the controlling officer and Accounts so an enquiry can be ordered; he cannot hide it or make it good quietly.

q: The 'dues' of a depot — the quantities of stores already on order with suppliers — are reviewed periodically mainly in order to:

options.A: Cancel or short-close orders for items which are no longer required, and thereby avoid excess procurement
options.B: Increase the closing balance of stores of the railway
options.C: Fix the book rate of the items on order
options.D: Prepare the catalogue for the next e-auction of scrap

e: Dues, meaning quantities already on order, are reviewed periodically so orders for items no longer required can be cancelled or short-closed, avoiding excess procurement and stock build-up.

q: A depot of one zonal railway despatches stores to a depot of another zonal railway against a transfer order. For the value of the material to be accounted for and settled between the two railways, the transaction is carried through:

options.A: Without any document, on the basis of a telephone message between the depots
options.B: On the basis of priced transfer notes, through the inter-railway transfer/adjustment accounts
options.C: By treating the material as sold in the open market
options.D: Only at the close of the financial year, in one lump sum for all transfers

e: Inter-railway transfers are accounted through priced transfer notes and settled through the inter-railway transfer and adjustment accounts, so both railways record the value correctly.

q: A stores item is purchased and Goods and Services Tax is paid on the purchase, input tax credit of the tax being available to the Railway. In taking the item into stock, the tax amount is:

options.A: Added in full to the book value of the stores in the Priced Stores Ledger
options.C: Not added to the cost of the stores, the credit being accounted for separately
options.D: Treated as part of the inventory carrying cost of the item

e: Where GST input tax credit is available, the tax is accounted for separately as credit and is not added to the cost or book value of stores in the Priced Stores Ledger.

q: Payment for supplies received from a micro or small enterprise is delayed beyond the period agreed or appointed under the MSMED Act. In such a case, the Railway as buyer is liable to pay:

options.A: Nothing over and above the bill amount
options.B: Double the amount of the bill, as penalty
options.C: Only a written apology to the supplier
options.D: Interest on the delayed payment, as provided in the Act

e: Under the MSMED Act, a buyer delaying payment to a micro or small enterprise beyond the agreed or appointed period is liable to pay interest on the delayed payment as provided in the Act.

q: For a high-value purchase, the tender documents require every bidder to sign a pact with the Railway, watched over by Independent External Monitors, under which neither side will indulge in corrupt practices in the procurement. Such a pact is known as:
e: The pact signed by bidders, overseen by Independent External Monitors, committing both sides against corrupt practices in procurement is the Integrity Pact.

q: A supplier, in support of a claim under the price variation clause of a stores contract, quotes figures of his input costs. The Accounts office is not satisfied with the figures as quoted and wishes to verify the costs and prices actually borne by the firm from its own records, as the contract permits. The clause of the contract which entitles the Railway to do so is the:
e: The book examination clause entitles the Railway to examine the supplier's own books and records to verify costs and prices claimed under the price variation clause.

q: A depot issues stores to a private firm for a purpose connected with the firm's work for the Railway, and the value of the stores so issued is to be recovered from the firm after final adjustment of the transaction. Pending that final adjustment and recovery, the value of the issue is held under the:
e: Issues to a private firm pending final adjustment and recovery are held under Stores Miscellaneous Suspense, which covers miscellaneous stores transactions awaiting clearance.

q: Tools and plant are issued from a depot to a department for use on works. The articles remain the property of the Railways, are accountable numerically by the department holding them, and are required to be returned after use. Such articles are borne on the:

options.C: Bin Card of the issuing depot

e: Tools and plant issued to departments remain Railway property, are accounted numerically by the holder and returned after use, so they are borne on the Dead Stock Register.

q: A depot officer is checking whether the receipt notes, issue notes, bin cards and stock sheets in use in his depot are the standard forms prescribed for stores depots on Indian Railways. These standard depot forms belong to the:
e: Standard forms used in stores depots, such as receipt notes, issue notes, bin cards and stock sheets, belong to the S-series of Indian Railways standard forms.

q: A stores depot of a zonal railway receives a new officer in charge. The designation of the officer in charge of a stores depot is:
e: The officer in charge of a stores depot is designated Depot Materials Superintendent, while the Controller of Stores heads the organisation at zonal headquarters.
